questions.question: Which analogy does the lesson use for an AI assistant?
options: A calculator that never makes mistakes
A very well-read new colleague who knows nothing about your company unless you tell them
A search engine that only returns links
A senior manager who knows your customers
questions.explanation: The lesson compares the assistant to a well-read colleague who joined today: quick and broadly informed, but without knowledge of your company, customers or deadline.

questions.question: What is a hallucination?
options: A response that is too long
A file the model cannot open
A confident-sounding answer that is false or made up
questions.explanation: The vocabulary table defines hallucination as a confident-sounding answer that is false or made up, which is why facts must be checked.

questions.question: In the Kaveri Home Loans example, what small error did the model make?
options: It wrote the email in the wrong language
It left out the subject line
It guessed that 5 November is a Wednesday
It addressed the email to customers
questions.explanation: The model invented a weekday for 5 November, a detail that may not match the actual year and must be checked before sending.

questions.question: Which is the right rule before pasting information into an AI tool at work?
options: Use only approved tools and never paste confidential data unless policy allows it
Any free public tool is fine for drafts
Paste customer PAN details if it saves time
Delete the chat afterwards and it is safe
questions.explanation: The rules of the road say to use approved tools and avoid confidential data such as PAN, Aadhaar, salaries or passwords unless company policy explicitly allows it.
